technical illustration · iso kit gallery

Anatomy collection, Part 3

Recreations of the anatomy collection's figures, rebuilt by the iso kit from JSON briefs, part 3. Each assembles on entry; hover or select a part to lift it.

Token bucket on an air bench

A recreation of anatomy's "Token bucket" (No. 27, Air bench) as an isometric air bench: a pump fills an orange token tank that holds at most eight tokens, a relief valve on the lid vents the overflow, and a punch press with an interlock spends one token for each punch of the paper tape.

Easing curves on a bench

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric easing bench: a lead screw moves a carriage at a constant rate (time); its follower, highlighted, rides a raised ease-in-out band on an upright graph plate, and a lift arm sets the element's height on the progress rail.

A strongbox with two kinds of key

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric strongbox with hinges, a hasp and a keyholed lid lock. Three public keys (bit, shaft, bow) lie on a rack on its left; one private key with an accented bow sits alone on a plinth on its right.

Pouring steel

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric foundry: a lined ladle on a trunnion, tilted by a hand wheel through a worm gearbox, pours a steel stream into the basin of a sand mould clamped on its bottom board. Hover or arrow keys lift a part.

The box model as a frame jig

A recreation of the anatomy collection's "Box model" frame jig. A picture-frame jig on a base, with a fence and a clamp, holds the CSS box model as nested frames: a dashed margin outline, a border moulding, a padding mat and the content print in orange. Hovering lifts the frames apart.

Branch and merge on a model railway

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric model railway: stations threaded on a main line, and a feature line that branches off and crosses back into main at the accented merge station, which has one stud per parent. Hover or arrow keys lift a part.

Pool reactor

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric TRIGA pool reactor in half section: a fuel core on a grid plate at the bottom of an open water tank, a control rod hanging from a drive on the bridge, and a console. The rod is highlighted; hover pulls it out.

One pane as a die set

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric die set: a base on four feet holds the picture bed; four guide pillars pass through the frosted copy, the ringed distance field and the glass pane on top, highlighted. A 2D canvas stands on the front ledge.

One context as a plotter

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric plotter: sixteen tiles, one 2D canvas per pane, each holding a stamped shape. A carriage on a back rail holds one print head over pane 16, and pane 15 beside it holds the image just stamped. Hover or arrow keys lift one part.

Shared canvas, a drafting board

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric drafting board in device pixels: a corner block at (0, 0), width and height rulers with ratchet stops marking a 512 by 352 canvas, and the accented draw card seated at the corner.

One texture, a tray of mip levels

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric tray: the picture stands in a slot at the back; eleven pockets in front, each narrower than the last, hold its mip levels down to a 1x1 pit. Three panes stand on the level matching their width; the frosted one is highlighted.

object-fit as a picture frame

After the anatomy collection. Dimetric picture frame on a steel square: the window is the element's box, the print fills it by cover, and the two overhanging strips lie cut off beside the frame. Hovering slides the cut strips away.

One stage as a chest of drawers

After the anatomy collection. Chest of seven render-target drawers: four tall half-float, three short 8-bit, glass pass output pill on top.
